chunks: My father narrated to me, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from some of our companions, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al- Askari (peace be upon them) on a Wednesday while he was having phlebotomy performed.

I said to him: The residents of the two Harams narrate on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Whoever has phlebotomy done on a Wednesday and suffers from white pigments (or blindness), let him blame only himself.' He replied: 'They lie. This only happens to those whose mothers were pregnant with them during menstruation.'

key_terms.بَيَاضٌ: Whiteness (often interpreted as blindness or loss of vision)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on phlebotomy on Wednesdays according to Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: Imam al-Askari (peace be upon him) refutes the popular superstition linking Wednesday cupping to 'whiteness' (often interpreted as blindness or vitiligo) by attributing the cause to the mother's menstrual state at conception, thereby shifting the focus from astrological timing to biological lineage. This critique highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between authentic medical or natural causes and cultural myths, reinforcing the principle that health outcomes are not bound to specific days of the week.
